paper.title_en: Accretion Flow Properties of MAXI J1834-021 during Its Multi-peaked Outburst in 2023
paper.abstract_en: The Galactic transient black hole candidate MAXI J1834-021 exhibited `faint' outburst activity for approximately $10$ months following its discovery on February 5, 2023. We study the evolution of both the temporal (hard and soft band photon count rates, hardness ratios, and QPO frequencies) and spectral properties of the source using NICER data between March 7 and October 4, 2023. The outburst profile and the nature of QPOs suggest that the source underwent a rebrightening following the primary episode of the outburst. A monotonic evolution of low-frequency QPOs from higher to lower frequencies is observed during the primary episode. Both phenomenological (diskbb plus powerlaw) and physical (Two Component Advective Flow) model fitted spectral studies suggest that during the entire epoch, the source remained in harder spectral states, with a clear dominance of nonthermal emissions from the `hot' Compton cloud. Based on the evolution of the spectral and temporal properties, the 2023 outburst activity of MAXI J1834-021 can be classified as a `failed' outburst, as no softer spectral states are observed. The spectral analysis with the TCAF model also gives an estimate of the source mass as $12.4\pm1.7~M_\odot$.
